biography: Frank Jelinski's journey began not on a racetrack, but in his father's autobody shop in rural Brandenburg. Surrounded by the scent of paint and the roar of engines, young Frank was captivated. His first taste of speed came in a rebuilt go-kart, terrorizing the local farmers' fields. This reckless abandon, surprisingly, caught the eye of a local karting coach. After years of honing his raw talent, he transitioned into Formula Ford, proving himself as a force to be reckoned with. An impressive performance in the Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch secured him a place in the Audi V8 quattro DTM team. Though he's still finding his footing, his aggressive driving style and undeniable speed have marked him as a rising star, albeit one prone to inconsistency.
drivingStyle: Jelinski is a high-risk, high-reward driver. He attacks corners with a ferocity that often leaves spectators gasping, bordering on recklessness. While this allows him to extract maximum performance from the car in short bursts, his tire management suffers, and he struggles to maintain consistent pace throughout an entire race. He thrives under pressure, often pulling off miraculous overtakes in the closing laps, but is equally prone to making costly mistakes when the stakes are high.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos dating back to their Formula Ford days; Richter views Jelinski as an undisciplined upstart, while Jelinski sees Richter as a boring, methodical driver.
Constant on-track battles, often resulting in close calls and accusations of aggressive driving. They respect each other's skill but refuse to yield an inch.
Teammates at Audi, Hoffman is frustrated with Jelinski's lack of consistency. He sees Jelinski as squandering valuable points for the team.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific German punk rock song before every race.
Has a habit of talking to his car, especially when it's misbehaving.
famousQuote: You either go flat out or you go home.
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula Ford Festival at Brands Hatch in a last-lap overtake that was deemed 'the most audacious move in Festival history' by commentators.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the DTM race at Hockenheim, costing Audi a potential 1-2 finish, due to an overly ambitious overtaking attempt.
